distillation_scope.leaf_granularity: first-layer clinical disease leaf for acute inflammatory myocardial injury, without splitting by viral, bacterial, fulminant, immune-checkpoint-inhibitor, eosinophilic, giant-cell, vaccine-associated, or autoimmune trigger subtype
distillation_scope.subtype_policy: Triggers and severity phenotypes are represented as latent mechanisms, context axes, risk factors, and treatment-effect modifiers, not as disease-name qualifiers.
distillation_scope.ranking_note: Presentation ranking should use prodrome, fever, chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, syncope/presyncope, shock physiology, troponin/CK, ECG changes, echocardiographic systolic dysfunction, pulmonary edema, and arrhythmia/conduction findings. CMR Lake Louise final read, endomyocardial biopsy/autopsy histology, viral PCR/serology, coronary angiography excluding ACS, treatment response, and outcome should be confirmatory or non-ranking unless a post-workup mode explicitly consumes them.

latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: A viral, bacterial, toxin/drug, vaccine-associated, immune-checkpoint-inhibitor, eosinophilic, giant-cell, or systemic autoimmune context activates myocardial innate and adaptive inflammation.

The trigger can produce fever, pharyngitis or upper respiratory symptoms, gastrointestinal symptoms, leukocytosis or leukopenia, high CRP, tachycardia, and malaise before or during cardiac presentation.
Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema in the myocardium alter repolarization, regional mechanics, myocardial strain, and CMR edema/LGE patterns.
Direct injury and immune-mediated myocyte necrosis release troponin, CK, LDH, and produce ECG patterns that can mimic acute coronary syndrome.
Subepicardial inflammation and adjacent pericardial involvement can cause sharp or pleuritic chest pain, positional pain, diffuse ST/T changes, and small pericardial effusion.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Acute ventricular dysfunction and heart failure
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Myocardial edema, myocyte injury, cytokine-mediated contractile depression, or fulminant inflammation can reduce LVEF, raise natriuretic peptide, cause pulmonary edema, dyspnea, low output, and end-organ hypoperfusion.
Inflammation or edema involving the AV node, His-Purkinje system, or nodal blood supply can produce PR prolongation, second- or third-degree AV block, bradycardia, dizziness, syncope, or pacing need.
Inflammation, necrosis, edema, autonomic stress, electrolyte disturbance, or scar substrate can provoke ectopy, ventricular tachycardia, atrial arrhythmia, malignant arrhythmia, or cardiac arrest.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Fulminant low-output shock and multiorgan injury
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: A severe acute inflammatory myocardial process can progress quickly to cardiogenic shock, respiratory failure from pulmonary edema, AKI, lactate elevation, need for mechanical circulatory support, and death.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Systemic inflammatory or infectious trigger activity raises CRP in many acute myocarditis presentations.
Cardiomyocyte injury makes qualitative troponin elevation clinically present even when exact assay scaling is not available.
Inflamed or edematous myocardium can produce focal or regional contractile abnormalities.
Myocarditis can mimic acute coronary syndrome while angiography shows no obstructive coronary lesion; stenosis presence should not be required for myocarditis.

Elevated troponin is direct myocardial injury support for acute myocarditis geometry. Acute myocarditis should require objective myocardial injury or inflammation context before its downstream physiology opens. Chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, panic symptoms, isolated AV block, shock physiology, pulmonary edema, or low ejection fraction alone are shared mimic geometry and should not unlock the myocarditis manifold.

Acute myocarditis with ventricular dysfunction can produce pulmonary venous congestion and pleural effusions.
Myocarditis-related heart failure can cause systemic venous congestion and peripheral edema.
Inflammatory myocardial and conduction-system involvement can produce nonspecific intraventricular conduction delay or bundle-branch-like delay.
Severe myocarditis with acute heart failure or hepatic congestion can elevate AST through congestive or hypoxic hepatopathy.
Severe myocarditis with acute heart failure or hepatic congestion can elevate ALT through congestive or hypoxic hepatopathy.
Fulminant low-output myocarditis can raise AST as part of ischemic or congestive hepatopathy.
Fulminant low-output myocarditis can raise ALT as part of ischemic or congestive hepatopathy.

axes.shape_free_text: C-reactive protein concentration reflecting systemic inflammatory activity that commonly accompanies acute myocarditis triggers or fulminant presentations.
Qualitative report that cardiac troponin is elevated when an exact assay-normalized value is unavailable.
Regional or segmental wall-motion abnormality on echocardiography or ventriculography in an acute myocardial injury syndrome.
Obstructive coronary artery stenosis on angiography; often absent in myocarditis that mimics acute coronary syndrome.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Reported fever and measured temperature often move together but may differ after antipyretics.
Inflammatory markers are commonly co-elevated, but viral and immune contexts may dissociate them.
Chest pain and troponin often coexist in infarct-like myocarditis but either can be absent.
Myocyte injury can produce ST/T abnormalities, but ECG sensitivity is incomplete.
Marked troponin elevation represents active myocardial injury.
Reduced LVEF raises acute heart failure risk.
Very low systolic reserve can progress to low-output shock.
Acute heart failure can cause pulmonary edema and congestion.
Pulmonary congestion is a direct dyspnea driver.
High-grade AV block commonly produces symptomatic bradycardia.
Second- and third-degree block define a high-grade block event state.
Complete AV block can cause low-output hypotension even when LVEF is near preserved.
Ventricular tachycardia is a direct marker of malignant arrhythmia hazard.
Unstable arrhythmia can lead to sudden death.
Cardiogenic shock is a major acute mortality pathway.
Low cardiac output and congestion can cause AKI.
Pulmonary edema, shock, and ventilatory fatigue can require respiratory support.

treatments.treatment_name: Heart failure and pulmonary congestion support

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Hypotension limits vasodilators and aggressive diuresis.
AKI or CKD reduces tolerance for diuresis and renin-angiotensin blockade.

treatments.treatment_name: Inotropes, vasopressors, and invasive hemodynamic support

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Catecholamines may worsen tachyarrhythmia while improving perfusion.
Low LVEF increases the need for contractile and perfusion support.
Persistent shock is the main context where mechanical support changes trajectory.
Circulatory support does not alone stabilize refractory ventricular arrhythmia.

toxicity_axis_effects.interpretation: Cannulation and anticoagulation increase bleeding risk.

treatments.role: reduce sudden electrical death risk during active myocarditis

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Antiarrhythmic and defibrillation benefit depends on active or threatened ventricular arrhythmia.
Electrolyte disturbance must be corrected to stabilize rhythm.

treatments.treatment_name: Temporary pacing for high-grade atrioventricular block
treatments.role: restore_rate_and_perfusion_when conduction block causes bradycardia or low output

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Pacing benefit is concentrated in high-grade block or symptomatic bradycardia.

treatments.role: reduce infectious trigger burden when a treatable pathogen or source is present

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Antibiotic effect depends on true treatable bacterial coverage.
Uncontrolled bacteremia source can sustain inflammatory myocardial injury.

treatments.role: reduce immune-mediated myocardial inflammation when immune, eosinophilic, giant-cell, ICI, or severe pediatric inflammatory context supports it

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: ICI myocarditis is an immune-mediated context where immunomodulation can be disease-reshaping.
Eosinophilic myocarditis is often steroid-responsive when infection is excluded or controlled.

treatments.treatment_name: Myopericarditis pain and pericardial inflammation control
treatments.role: reduce epicardial/pericardial pain and inflammation when pericardial features dominate and ventricular dysfunction is not severe

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: NSAID-style pain strategies may be less attractive in significant heart failure.

supportive_care.description: Continuous ECG, blood pressure, oxygenation, urine output, lactate, and serial cardiac biomarker monitoring during active or unstable disease.
Avoid strenuous exercise during active inflammation and biomarker/ECG instability.
Repeat echocardiography to track ventricular function, effusion, congestion, and recovery or worsening.
Correct potassium, magnesium, renal perfusion, and acid-base problems that amplify arrhythmia and shock risk.
CMR, coronary evaluation, endomyocardial biopsy, viral/immune testing, and trigger search can refine context after presentation ranking.

quality_notes: The disease name is deliberately trigger-agnostic. Viral, bacterial, fulminant, ICI, eosinophilic, autoimmune, and vaccine-associated contexts are mechanisms or modifiers.
No first_line, preferred, guideline_recommended, diagnosis_should_be, or single-case label fields are used.
CMR and biopsy axes exist for post-workup structure but should be kept non-ranking in presentation-only case JSON unless the test mode explicitly includes confirmatory evidence.
